assessment_question: What are Sealed Classes in Java?
initial_response: In Java, sealed classes are a feature introduced in Java 15 (preview) and standardized in Java 17. They allow you to control which classes can extend or implement a given class or interface, giving you more precise control over inheritance.
followup_question: How do sealed classes provide better control over inheritance hierarchies?
followup_response: Sealed classes give you fine-grained control over inheritance hierarchies by explicitly declaring which classes are allowed to extend or implement them. This prevents “accidental” or “unauthorized” subclassing and makes the design of your type system much clearer.
